question: A 23-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his girlfriend because of acute agitation and bizarre behavior. The girlfriend reports that, over the past 3 months, the patient has become withdrawn and stopped pursuing hobbies that he used to enjoy. One month ago, he lost his job because he stopped going to work. During this time, he has barely left his apartment because he believes that the FBI is spying on him and controlling his mind. He used to smoke marijuana occasionally in high school but quit 5 years ago. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. On mental status examination, he is confused and suspicious with marked psychomotor agitation. His speech is disorganized and his affect is labile. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Belief that FBI is spying on him and controlling his mind -> Delusions -> Paranoia -> Suspiciousness -> Confusion -> Disorganized speech -> Labile affect -> Psychomotor agitation -> Acute agitation and bizarre behavior -> Brief psychotic disorder -> 95%

CHAIN: Withdrawn behavior and loss of interest in hobbies -> Social withdrawal -> Occupational impairment -> Delusional beliefs -> Confusion -> Disorganized speech -> Labile affect -> Psychomotor agitation -> Acute agitation and bizarre behavior -> Brief psychotic disorder -> 90%
analysis: The patient is presenting with acute agitation, bizarre behavior, delusions of persecution, and disorganized speech, which are characteristic symptoms of schizophrenia. The duration of symptoms for more than 1 month rules out brief psychotic disorder. Schizoaffective disorder involves a combination of mood symptoms and psychotic features, which are not prominent in this case. Schizoid personality disorder is characterized by a long-standing pattern of detachment from social relationships and limited emotional expression, which does not fit the acute presentation described. Schizophreniform disorder is similar to schizophrenia but has a duration of symptoms between 1 to 6 months, making it a less likely diagnosis. Delusional disorder typically involves non-bizarre delusions without other prominent psychotic symptoms seen in this case.
